question: Does WooCommerce Subscriptions Work on a Marketplace Plugin?
metaDescription: WooCommerce Subscriptions can work on a multi-vendor marketplace two different ways — vendor plans and vendor-sold products, each with different setup needs.
shortAnswer: It depends which of two different things you mean: charging vendors a recurring fee to sell on the marketplace (most marketplace plugins like Dokan and WCFM have their own dedicated vendor-subscription systems for this, separate from WooCommerce Subscriptions), versus letting individual vendors sell subscription products to customers, which generally does work through WooCommerce Subscriptions but needs checking against the specific marketplace plugin's commission and payout handling for recurring orders.

bodyHtml:
Two Different Things Called "Marketplace Subscriptions"

Marketplace plugins like Dokan and WCFM typically ship their own vendor membership/subscription system for charging sellers to access the marketplace (a monthly seller fee, for instance) — that's usually independent of WooCommerce Subscriptions entirely, run through the marketplace plugin's own billing. Separately, individual vendors can list and sell subscription products to customers, which does go through WooCommerce Subscriptions if it's active, subject to how the marketplace plugin splits commissions on recurring orders specifically.

Where This Gets Complicated

  • Commission handling on renewal orders. A marketplace plugin's commission logic built primarily for one-time orders doesn't always split a renewal order correctly by default — worth testing a full renewal cycle, not just the initial sale.
  • Vendor payout timing for recurring revenue. Confirm whether the marketplace plugin's payout schedule correctly picks up renewal-order commissions on an ongoing basis, not just the first purchase.
  • Which subscription statuses trigger a payout — a refunded or disputed renewal needs its commission handled correctly too, not just successful charges.
  • Vendor-side management of their own subscription products, confirming the vendor dashboard actually exposes the subscription-specific product fields (billing interval, trial, sign-up fee) rather than only generic product fields.

How to Verify It Properly

  1. Clarify which type of "subscription" is actually needed — vendor fees, or vendor-sold subscription products — since they're solved completely differently.
  2. Test a full renewal cycle on a vendor-sold subscription product, confirming commission splits and vendor payouts both work correctly on the second and later charges, not just the first.
  3. Check the specific marketplace plugin's own documentation for explicit WooCommerce Subscriptions compatibility notes, since support varies by plugin and version.

See custom WooCommerce development for marketplace commission logic on recurring orders that needs custom handling.
